author: GNiendorf
body:
This PR builds LSTCore with fast floating-point flags:
- serial backend: `ofast-flag` (`-Ofast -fno-reciprocal-math`), as MkFitCore and PixelSeeding already do;
- CUDA backend: `--use_fast_math`.

Two lines in `RecoTracker/LSTCore/BuildFile.xml`.

#### Validation
On SegmentLinking master (IB CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-10-07-1100) with only this PR, Phase-2 HLT, 500 ttbar + 500 QCD PU200 events:
- Efficiency, fake and duplicate rates of hltGeneralTracks agree within statistics on the CPU and on the GPU. **Numerical precision-level differences are expected from the flags.** MTV (CPU): [ttbar](https://gniendorf.github.io/lst-plots/internal-prs/lst-build-flags/ttbar/plots_hlt.html), [QCD](https://gniendorf.github.io/lst-plots/internal-prs/lst-build-flags/qcd/plots_hlt.html).
- Timing, 16 jobs x 16 threads (AMD EPYC 9654, NVIDIA L40): hltLST 35.9 -> 29.4 ms per event in the GPU menu (-18%) and 882 -> 837 ms in the CPU menu (-5%), means of two alternating rounds.
title: LSTCore: -Ofast for the CPU backend and --use_fast_math for CUDA
